declarations.checkedType: agent(body: unknown, context: string, url: string) -> unknown with throw[api_error | auth_error | fetch_error | parse_error] | credential | io
declarations.documentation:
POST @body@ to the Tavily @url@ with the credential, and hand back the reply's parsed document — the
one wire call this package makes, so the classification happens once, at the boundary that produced
the status. A non-2xx arrives as the transport's `http.status_error` and leaves as `http.api_failure`,
drawn by `http.classify_status`: a 401/403 is the CREDENTIAL failing (`http.auth_error`, which a
`replay` converter turns into a fresh resolution of it, and, when it cannot be refreshed, the
runtime's re-authorization park), every other non-2xx is an `http.api_error` — a rejected query, a
rate limit, an exhausted credit balance, a server fault. @context@ names the failing call for a human,
the server's own body rides as the message, and the STATUS rides onward, so a retry policy downstream
reads a number rather than searching a sentence. A transport failure (`http.fetch_error`) and a 2xx
that is not JSON (`json.parse_error`) are not statuses to classify, so the residual rethrows them as
bound.
declarations.name: post

anyOf.description:
api_error: An authenticated API call failed for anything OTHER than the credential: a non-2xx @status@ that is not
401/403 — a malformed request, a resource that is not there, a rate limit, a server error. Nothing about
the caller's identity is in question, so backing off and replaying the call AS IT STANDS is the whole
recovery for the transient half, and the other half (a 400 the service is simply refusing) will keep
failing until the ARGUMENT changes.

WHICH half a given failure is, is read off @status@ and nowhere else: 408 / 429 / 5xx are the transient
ones a retry policy should back off and repeat, every other status is a refusal that will repeat forever.
That is the whole reason the status RIDES on the error instead of being folded into a sentence — a retry
policy downstream reads a number, never a message.

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words; @message@ carries the server's own body
verbatim, because it is the diagnosis and a model handed this error reads it and adjusts.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "tavily.search").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
auth_error: An authenticated API call was rejected over WHO IS CALLING: the endpoint answered @status@ — 401 or
403 — so the CREDENTIAL is what failed: revoked, expired past what its holder believed, or scoped too
narrowly for this call. Retrying with the SAME credential cannot succeed; the recovery is a fresh
RESOLUTION of it, which is why the ordinary composition is a `replay` converter that signals
`replay.interrupted`: the re-run resolves the credential again, and one the runtime cannot refresh parks
the run on a `prelude.oauth.authorize` escalation — a human's re-authorization prompt — rather than
failing. That is the whole line this variant draws: an `auth_error` may need a HUMAN before any retry can
work, an `api_error` never does.

(403 is read as auth even though some APIs also spend it on quota exhaustion. The access-rejection reading
is the one worth composing a re-resolution around, and a quota 403 that is replayed simply fails again.)

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words, and @message@ carries the server's own body —
the two halves a human needs, kept apart so a renderer can show either without splitting a string.

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

fetch_error: An HTTP request never completed: DNS failure, refused connection, timeout, or a mid-flight runtime
restart. Thrown by `fetch`. (A response that did arrive is never an error — branch on its `status`.)

declarations.checkedType: agent(max_results?: integer, query: string) -> array[result] with throw[api_error | auth_error | fetch_error | parse_error] | credential | io
declarations.documentation:
Search the web and return the top hits as structured results — a value the program can route
(follow the urls, filter, rank) rather than a pre-rendered string. A reply without the promised
`results` array degrades to the empty list (the API never contractually promised the shape); a failed
call is `http.api_failure` (`http.auth_error` for a 401/403, `http.api_error` otherwise).
declarations.name: search
